page: Amazon Web Services r6i.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance alongside average single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions and encryption, as well as strong multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only large block transfers reaching 338.62 GB/sec. However, single-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core, fall into the average category, highlighting a tradeoff where massive parallelization outperforms individual core speed.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bare-metal architecture eliminates virtualization overhead, maximizing the return on the 1024.0 GB memory allocation for resource-dense deployments. This profile is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale databases, Redis enterprise clusters, and high-throughput static web serving. It is also capable of handling moderate LLM inference tasks, particularly prompt processing, though text generation speeds remain average.
